name: The Fairmont Copley Plaza
insider_take: This iconic Boston landmark has been the city's "Grand Dame" since 1912, where old-world elegance meets modern luxury in the heart of Back Bay.
whats_special: The Fairmont Copley Plaza sits on the original site of the Museum of Fine Arts and features a stunning rooftop beehive producing honey served in the hotel's restaurants. The lobby's magnificent coffered ceiling and crystal chandeliers have welcomed presidents, celebrities, and dignitaries for over a century. The hotel's resident canine ambassadors, Fairmont Gold Retrievers Carly Simon and James Taylor, add a charming Boston touch.
pro_tip: Book a room facing Copley Square for prime views of Trinity Church's stunning Romanesque architecture - it's particularly magical when illuminated at night.
dont_miss: Step outside to explore Copley Square's architectural treasures including Trinity Church and the Boston Public Library's McKim Building. The hotel is perfectly positioned for Back Bay shopping along Newbury Street and just steps from the finish line of the legendary Boston Marathon on Boylston Street.
pros: Iconic Beaux-Arts landmark in the heart of Boston's historic Back Bay neighborhood
Unbeatable location steps from Copley Square, the Boston Marathon finish line, and world-class shopping on Newbury Street
Elegantly appointed rooms and suites showcasing grand historic architecture with modern luxury amenities
Acclaimed dining at OAK Long Bar + Kitchen, celebrated for craft cocktails, seasonal New England cuisine, and vibrant atmosphere
Storied history and refined service tradition dating to 1912, beloved by presidents, celebrities, and discerning travelers
cons: Premium urban pricing reflective of its landmark status and prime Back Bay location
No on-site pool or spa facility; guests seeking resort-style wellness amenities should plan accordingly
